The front end

Dashboard, trial explorer, trial detail, ⌘K search and settings, in React with shadcn/ui. Every page runs on the real API over all 607,349 trials, in light and dark, on a phone or a wide screen. Nothing is committed yet.

Page map

Four pages and a palette, linked by the filter

The URL carries the filter in the API's own format, so a link is the view, and the dashboard and the trial list show the same slice.

Screens

What each page looks like

Light theme, 1440 px wide, real data. The tops of the pages; the next slide has dark and phone.

Both themes, every width

Dark mode and phones

The theme follows the system until you pick one (header button, Settings or ⌘K); it's set before the first paint, so a dark page never flashes white. No page scrolls sideways at 375 px.

How the UI gets its data

Typed from the schema, cached until the data changes

The Update button, live

Progress streams in; the page refreshes itself

Update now POST /api/jobs/update

202 with the job, or 409 with the one already queued or running; the page follows that one.

The worker runs it app.db, 2×/s

Stage, done/total and message, read by the event stream every half second.

The card and the job list move SSE job events

A bar when the total is known, elapsed time, Cancel. The sidebar shows a spinner on every page.

It commits SSE data_version

Every data query refetches; a toast and the header say “Data updated just now”.

I pressed it once to check this: one real no-change update (job #2). The data-version path, which a no-change run doesn't trigger, is checked by a Playwright test with a stand-in event stream and by unit tests.

4 · the widget registry

  • statstat tiles
  • barRecharts bars
  • line, areaRecharts, crosshair
  • piedonut + legend
  • tablea table
  • maplazy chunk (d3-geo)
  • anything elsea placeholder

Width is on a 4-column grid (2 on tablets, 1 on phones); every chart has a table view, and takes the page's filter.

The map widget

d3-geo and world-atlas, in its own 12 KB chunk

Below: dark, filtered to Alzheimer's (3 classes, spread over the whole ramp so they still differ).

Why this library

Projection and paths only, drawn as SVG: the same theme colors and tooltips as the other charts, offline (no tile server), maintained (d3-geo 3.1). The shapes are a separate 40 KB file, cached.

Not chosen

react-simple-maps (unmaintained, no React 19); Leaflet or MapLibre (tiles, or 200 KB+); nivo's geo (several d3 bundles).

How it reads

One blue ramp in decade classes (1+, 10+ … 100K+), since counts span five orders of magnitude. Hong Kong, Singapore and 30 other places too small for the shapes are dots. Hover the list or a country; click opens its trials.

Against the targets (§10)

Both budgets met, with room

JavaScript, gzip

npm run budget, from Vite's manifest

Initial JS is what every page needs before it draws. Recharts (119 KB) comes with the dashboard, so a cold dashboard load fetches 289 KB; the 1.5 s target covers that whole load. Lazy toasts and a one-button theme toggle took the entry from 145 to 125 KB.

Dashboard on a cold load

5 runs, new browser context each, Chrome 155, tri-al serve on 607k trials

"Interactive" is every chart from /api/dashboard drawn, the map included, timed from navigation. The server's share is about 5 ms; the rest is downloading and running the JS.

Checks, and what changed on the server

Everything passes

Web (new CI job)

  • Biome lint and format, tsc strict
  • the generated client matches the API (npm run api:check)
  • 40 Vitest tests: filters ↔ URL, the event stream, widgets and placeholder, ⌘K and capped, facets, job progress, changes
  • build, then the bundle budget

Playwright, on the installed database (local)

  • dashboard → filter → trial detail → ⌘K, typing before the palette has opened
  • settings; a new data version over the stream refreshes the page
  • the cold-load budget

Python: 581 tests, ruff, strict mypy

17 new tests for the changes below.

Small API changes

  • Typed schema: the OpenAPI schema said string for every response, because JSONBytes wasn't a JSONResponse. Now it is, and a test checks each route has its model.
  • /api/meta sends labels for coded fields, so the UI keeps no copy.
  • The SPA on the API's port (tri_al.api.web, server.web_dir).
  • python -m tri_al.api.openapi exports the core's schema for codegen.
